questions.questionText: [Section A] Mrs Banda lives with her husband, their five children, and her elderly mother, who all share one home. Name the type of family shown.
questions.correctAnswer: Extended family
questions.explanation: The household includes members beyond the nuclear family (a grandparent), making it an extended family.

questions.questionText: [Section A] Give one other type of family found in communities besides the one named above.
questions.correctAnswer: Nuclear family, single-parent family, child-headed family, polygamous family, or blended family
questions.explanation: Common family types found in communities include nuclear, single-parent, child-headed, polygamous and blended families.

questions.questionText: [Section A] State one reason why keeping cattle is valuable to a rural family.
questions.correctAnswer: Cattle provide draught power, milk, meat, manure, and can be sold for income.
questions.explanation: Cattle serve multiple economic and cultural purposes for rural households.

questions.questionText: [Section A] Identify one way family members can depend on each other.
questions.correctAnswer: Sharing household chores, financial support, emotional support, or caring for each other when sick.
questions.explanation: Family members support each other through shared responsibilities and mutual care.

questions.questionText: [Section A] Suggest one reason why family roles are important in the community.
questions.correctAnswer: Clear roles help the family function smoothly and contribute positively to the wider community's stability.
questions.explanation: Well-defined family roles support both household functioning and broader social order.

questions.questionText: [Section A] Give one way a person can be physically abused.
questions.correctAnswer: Being beaten, hit, or injured by another person.
questions.explanation: Physical abuse involves inflicting bodily harm on a person.

questions.questionText: [Section A] State one action a learner who is being abused at school should take.
questions.correctAnswer: Report the abuse to a trusted teacher, the school head, or a parent/guardian.
questions.explanation: Reporting to a trusted adult is the recommended first step when facing abuse.

questions.questionText: [Section A] Name one way religion can help a person who has suffered abuse.
questions.correctAnswer: Providing emotional/spiritual support, counselling, and a caring community for healing.
questions.explanation: Religious communities often provide counselling and emotional support to those affected by abuse.

questions.questionText: [Section A] List one substance that can be abused.
questions.correctAnswer: Alcohol, tobacco, or illegal drugs
questions.explanation: Commonly abused substances include alcohol, tobacco and illicit drugs.

questions.questionText: [Section A] Identify one way a community can assist people who abuse substances.
questions.correctAnswer: Referring them for counselling/rehabilitation and providing community support programmes.
questions.explanation: Communities can help by connecting affected individuals with counselling and rehabilitation services.

questions.questionText: [Section A] Give one example of a pre-colonial state that existed in the region now called Zimbabwe.
questions.correctAnswer: Mutapa State, Rozvi State, or Torwa State
questions.explanation: Mutapa, Rozvi and Torwa were major pre-colonial states in the region.

questions.questionText: [Section A] Name Zimbabwe's national coat of arms, which displays symbols such as kudus and a bird.
questions.correctAnswer: The National Coat of Arms
questions.explanation: The described symbol is Zimbabwe's National Coat of Arms.

questions.questionText: [Section A] State what the kudus on the national coat of arms are generally understood to represent.
questions.correctAnswer: Grace, alertness and the natural wildlife heritage of Zimbabwe.
questions.explanation: Kudus are included as supporters on the coat of arms, associated with grace and vigilance.

questions.questionText: [Section A] State one cause of the first Chimurenga/Umvukela.
questions.correctAnswer: Resistance to colonial rule and the loss of land and cattle to settlers.
questions.explanation: The uprising was largely triggered by anger over land dispossession and colonial oppression.

questions.questionText: [Section A] Give one example of an indigenous court found in Zimbabwe.
questions.correctAnswer: The dare/inkundla (traditional chief's or headman's court)
questions.explanation: The dare/inkundla is a customary court used to resolve community disputes.

questions.questionText: [Section A] Name one natural resource found in Zimbabwe.
questions.correctAnswer: Water, forests, minerals (e.g., gold), or wildlife.
questions.explanation: Zimbabwe has several natural resources including water bodies, forests, minerals and wildlife.

questions.questionText: [Section A] State one reason for conserving natural resources.
questions.correctAnswer: To ensure resources remain available for future generations and to protect the environment.
questions.explanation: Conservation ensures sustainable use of resources over time.

questions.questionText: [Section A] The process of replanting trees in an area which previously had trees is called
questions.correctAnswer: Reforestation
questions.explanation: Reforestation is specifically the replanting of trees in a previously forested area.

questions.questionText: [Section A] Identify one effect of veld fires on the environment.
questions.correctAnswer: Destruction of vegetation, loss of wildlife habitat, and soil left bare and exposed to erosion.
questions.explanation: Veld fires destroy plant cover and can harm animals and soil quality.

questions.questionText: [Section A] Suggest one way of overcoming desertification.
questions.correctAnswer: Planting trees and grass, and practising controlled grazing to protect soil cover.
questions.explanation: Restoring vegetation cover helps reverse the spread of desert-like conditions.

questions.questionText: [Section A] State one reason why spitting in a public place is a bad practice.
questions.correctAnswer: It can spread germs/diseases to other people.
questions.explanation: Spitting in public can transmit disease-causing microorganisms to others.

questions.questionText: [Section A] Give one example of a communicable disease.
questions.correctAnswer: Tuberculosis, cholera, influenza, or COVID-19.
questions.explanation: Communicable diseases are those that can spread from person to person.

questions.questionText: [Section A] State one career that can be considered a good choice in a person's lifetime.
questions.correctAnswer: Teaching, nursing, engineering, farming, or any legitimate profession the learner values.
questions.explanation: A good career choice depends on personal interest and the value it brings to society, and can include many professions.

questions.questionText: [Section A] Explain why the career you named above is considered good.
questions.correctAnswer: It provides income, serves the community, and matches the person's skills/interests.
questions.explanation: A good career typically offers both a livelihood and a meaningful contribution to society.

questions.questionText: [Section A] Define the term 'vandalism'.
questions.correctAnswer: The deliberate destruction or damage of property.
questions.explanation: Vandalism refers to intentionally damaging or destroying property belonging to others or the public.

questions.questionText: [Section B] Name one of the twelve disciples of Jesus Christ.
questions.correctAnswer: Peter, John, James, Andrew, or any other of the twelve disciples.
questions.explanation: The twelve disciples included figures such as Peter, John, James and Andrew.

questions.questionText: [Section B] Give the meaning of the word 'parable' as used in Jesus' teachings.
questions.correctAnswer: A short, simple story used to illustrate a moral or spiritual lesson.
questions.explanation: A parable is a teaching method using a relatable story to convey a deeper meaning.

questions.questionText: [Section B] Describe briefly how Jesus Christ was put to death, according to Christian teaching.
questions.correctAnswer: He was crucified (nailed to a cross) after being tried and condemned.
questions.explanation: Christian teaching holds that Jesus was crucified on a cross in Jerusalem.

questions.questionText: [Section B] State the city where Jesus Christ was crucified.
questions.correctAnswer: Jerusalem
questions.explanation: Christian tradition places the crucifixion of Jesus in Jerusalem.

questions.questionText: [Section B] Give the name of the person regarded as the founder of the Israelite/Jewish nation and its covenant with God.
questions.correctAnswer: Abraham (or Moses, associated with receiving the Torah)
questions.explanation: Abraham is considered the patriarchal founder of the Israelite nation; Moses is central to receiving the Torah.

questions.questionText: [Section B] Name the six-pointed star widely recognised as a symbol of Judaism.
questions.correctAnswer: The Star of David (Magen David)
questions.explanation: The Star of David is the most widely recognised symbol of Judaism.

questions.questionText: [Section B] Give one ceremony practised in the Jewish religion.
questions.correctAnswer: Bar Mitzvah/Bat Mitzvah, Brit Milah (circumcision), or Passover Seder.
questions.explanation: Jewish religious ceremonies include Bar/Bat Mitzvah, Brit Milah and festival observances such as Passover.

questions.questionText: [Section B] Jews traditionally worship in a place called a
questions.correctAnswer: Synagogue
questions.explanation: The synagogue is the traditional place of Jewish communal worship.

questions.questionText: [Section B] Name the religion in which male circumcision is performed as a religious rite shortly after birth.
questions.correctAnswer: Judaism (Brit Milah) — also practised in Islam
questions.explanation: Judaism performs circumcision (Brit Milah) on the eighth day after a boy's birth as a religious rite; Islam also practises circumcision.

questions.questionText: [Section B] Name the two main branches/groups within Islam.
questions.correctAnswer: Sunni and Shi'a
questions.explanation: Islam is mainly divided into the Sunni and Shi'a branches.

questions.questionText: [Section B] State one ceremony/festival celebrated in the Islamic religion.
questions.correctAnswer: Eid al-Fitr or Eid al-Adha
questions.explanation: Muslims celebrate festivals such as Eid al-Fitr (end of Ramadan) and Eid al-Adha.

questions.questionText: [Section B] Name one group of religious practitioners found in Islam.
questions.correctAnswer: Imams
questions.explanation: Imams lead prayer and provide religious guidance in Islam.

questions.questionText: [Section B] Muslims pray facing the direction of a sacred site called the
questions.correctAnswer: Kaaba (in Mecca)
questions.explanation: Muslim prayer (Salah) is directed towards the Kaaba located in Mecca.

questions.questionText: [Section B] Identify one of the Five Pillars of Islam.
questions.correctAnswer: Shahada, Salah, Zakat, Sawm, or Hajj.
questions.explanation: The Five Pillars of Islam are Shahada, Salah, Zakat, Sawm and Hajj.

questions.questionText: [Section B] Give the name of a sacred/special place traditionally found within a homestead in Indigenous Religion.
questions.correctAnswer: The chikuva (family shrine/altar area) or a sacred family site.
questions.explanation: Many Zimbabwean homesteads traditionally have a sacred spot associated with ancestral veneration.

questions.questionText: [Section B] Name one group of religious practitioners found in Indigenous Religion.
questions.correctAnswer: Spirit mediums/n'anga, or traditional healers.
questions.explanation: Spirit mediums and traditional healers are key religious practitioners in Indigenous Religion.

questions.questionText: [Section B] State the name of any one national ancestor recognised in Zimbabwe.
questions.correctAnswer: Mbuya Nehanda or Sekuru Kaguvi (examples of recognised national ancestors/spirit mediums).
questions.explanation: Nehanda and Kaguvi are widely recognised national ancestral/spirit figures in Zimbabwean history.

questions.questionText: [Section B] Identify one traditional artefact associated with Indigenous Religion.
questions.correctAnswer: A calabash, clay pot, walking stick, or beads used in ritual practice.
questions.explanation: Traditional artefacts such as calabashes and ritual beads are associated with Indigenous Religion practices.

questions.questionText: [Section B] State one way HIV can be contracted.
questions.correctAnswer: Unprotected sexual intercourse, contact with infected blood, or mother-to-child transmission.
questions.explanation: HIV is transmitted mainly through unprotected sex, blood contact, or from mother to child.

questions.questionText: [Section B] Identify one way of preventing HIV and AIDS.
questions.correctAnswer: Abstinence, being faithful to one partner, using condoms correctly, or avoiding sharing sharp objects.
questions.explanation: Prevention methods include abstinence, faithfulness, condom use, and avoiding unsafe practices involving blood.

questions.questionText: [Section B] State one way learners whose parents are living with HIV and AIDS may be affected.
questions.correctAnswer: They may face emotional stress, reduced financial support, or increased household responsibilities.
questions.explanation: Children in such households often take on additional responsibilities and may experience emotional strain.

questions.questionText: [Section B] State one circle of sexuality besides reproduction.
questions.correctAnswer: Sensuality, intimacy, sexual identity, or sexualisation.
questions.explanation: The circles of sexuality typically include sensuality, intimacy, sexual identity and reproduction, among others.

questions.questionText: [Section B] Explain what 'reproduction' means as one of the circles of sexuality.
questions.correctAnswer: The biological process by which living things, including humans, produce offspring.
questions.explanation: Reproduction refers to how organisms, including humans, create new generations.

questions.questionText: [Section C] Name one indigenous hunting tool historically used in Zimbabwe.
questions.correctAnswer: Bow and arrow, spear, or trap/snare.
questions.explanation: Traditional hunters in Zimbabwe used tools such as bows, spears and snares.

questions.questionText: [Section C] Identify one material traditionally used to make indigenous hunting tools.
questions.correctAnswer: Wood, iron/metal, or animal sinew.
questions.explanation: Hunting tools were traditionally crafted from wood, metal and natural fibres such as sinew.

questions.questionText: [Section C] Name one occasion that symbolises a rite of passage.
questions.correctAnswer: Initiation ceremony, marriage, or a coming-of-age ceremony.
questions.explanation: Rites of passage mark important transitions such as initiation or marriage.

questions.questionText: [Section C] Identify the person typically responsible for overseeing the sharing of a deceased person's property in Indigenous Religion/custom.
questions.correctAnswer: A family elder or the deceased's next of kin, often guided by customary practice.
questions.explanation: Customary inheritance matters are usually overseen by senior family members according to tradition.

questions.questionText: [Section C] State an indigenous ritual ceremony performed about a year after the death of a family member.
questions.correctAnswer: Kurova guva
questions.explanation: Kurova guva is performed roughly a year after death to welcome the deceased's spirit as an ancestor.

questions.questionText: [Section C] State one cause of drought.
questions.correctAnswer: Prolonged low or erratic rainfall, often worsened by climate change.
questions.explanation: Droughts result mainly from extended periods without sufficient rainfall.

questions.questionText: [Section C] Identify one effect of drought on communities.
questions.correctAnswer: Crop failure, food shortages, water scarcity, or loss of livestock.
questions.explanation: Drought commonly leads to reduced harvests, water shortages, and livestock losses.

questions.questionText: [Section C] Give one way of reducing poverty in Zimbabwe.
questions.correctAnswer: Promoting education, supporting small businesses/entrepreneurship, or improving access to farming inputs.
questions.explanation: Poverty reduction strategies include improving education, supporting livelihoods, and agricultural support.

questions.questionText: [Section C] Name the form of pollution caused by scattered plastic bottles, papers and other rubbish on the ground.
questions.correctAnswer: Land pollution
questions.explanation: Solid waste littering the land surface is classified as land pollution.

questions.questionText: [Section C] Suggest one way of preventing land pollution.
questions.correctAnswer: Proper waste disposal, recycling, and community clean-up campaigns.
questions.explanation: Managing waste responsibly through disposal and recycling helps prevent land pollution.

questions.questionText: [Section C] State the approximate gestation period of a human.
questions.correctAnswer: About nine months (approximately 280 days)
questions.explanation: Human pregnancy (gestation) lasts around nine months.

questions.questionText: [Section C] State one advantage of immunising babies.
questions.correctAnswer: It protects babies from serious, sometimes fatal, childhood diseases.
questions.explanation: Immunisation builds immunity against diseases that can seriously harm infants.

questions.questionText: [Section C] Explain why a mother's breast milk is considered the best food for a newborn baby.
questions.correctAnswer: It contains the right balance of nutrients and antibodies that protect the baby from infections.
questions.explanation: Breast milk provides ideal nutrition along with antibodies that boost a baby's immune system.

questions.questionText: [Section C] State one purpose of a traditional courtship practice where families exchange tokens or gifts before marriage.
questions.correctAnswer: To show the seriousness of the intention to marry and to begin building ties between the two families.
questions.explanation: Exchanging tokens during courtship formalises intent and starts building relations between families.

questions.questionText: [Section C] State one role played by aunts or uncles during courtship in Zimbabwean culture.
questions.correctAnswer: Advising and guiding the couple, and representing the family during marriage negotiations.
questions.explanation: Aunts and uncles traditionally play advisory and mediating roles during courtship and marriage arrangements.

questions.questionText: [Section C] State one example of responsible behaviour a worker can show at their workplace.
questions.correctAnswer: Being punctual, honest, and completing assigned tasks properly.
questions.explanation: Responsible workplace behaviour includes punctuality, honesty and diligence.

questions.questionText: [Section C] Name the association responsible for administering football in Zimbabwe.
questions.correctAnswer: Zimbabwe Football Association (ZIFA)
questions.explanation: ZIFA is the governing body overseeing football in Zimbabwe.

questions.questionText: [Section C] Identify one area/branch of art.
questions.correctAnswer: Painting, sculpture, music, drama, or dance.
questions.explanation: Art includes various branches such as painting, sculpture, music and drama.

questions.questionText: [Section C] Name one item of protective clothing a welder should wear.
questions.correctAnswer: A welding mask/visor, gloves, or protective overalls.
questions.explanation: Welders wear protective gear such as masks and gloves to protect against sparks and heat.

questions.questionText: [Section C] Identify the type of material welders commonly use to produce a variety of items.
questions.correctAnswer: Metal (iron/steel)
questions.explanation: Welding is done on metal materials such as iron and steel to join or shape them into items.
